claims.text: Atomic-scale homogeneous distribution of Pt, Pd, Rh, Ru, Ir, and Os enhances ethanol oxidation selectivity.
Atomic-scale homogeneous distribution of Pt, Pd, Rh, Ru, Ir, and Os enhances catalyst durability during ethanol oxidation.
Homogeneity prevents localized over-oxidation of oxidation-prone elements that would otherwise block active sites.
The initial nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst is a uniformly alloyed solid solution with no detectable phase segregation.
The initial catalyst has no significant surface oxide gradients under the stated synthesis conditions.
Reducing-atmosphere thermal annealing is intended to induce partial phase segregation into element-enriched nanodomains.
The relevant structural mediator is the surface atomic distribution of the alloying elements, specifically homogeneity versus phase segregation.
A uniform PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solution tunes the constituent metals' d-band centers.
The proposed d-band tuning suppresses over-oxidation of susceptible elements during ethanol oxidation.
Suppressing over-oxidation keeps active sites in their metallic state.
Phase segregation creates local regions in which oxidation-prone metals oxidize prematurely.
Premature oxidation in segregated regions blocks active sites and reduces catalytic performance.
Homogeneous catalysts will exhibit higher ethanol oxidation current densities than partially segregated catalysts.
Homogeneous catalysts will exhibit a more favorable product distribution with fewer over-oxidation side products than partially segregated catalysts.
Homogeneous catalysts will exhibit greater durability under prolonged ethanol oxidation than partially segregated catalysts.
The proposed relationship is expected to hold in acidic ethanol oxidation media at 60–100°C under typical laboratory operating regimes.
A Co-Mo-Fe-Ni-Cu HEA catalyst showed negligible activity degradation over approximately 50 hours of ammonia decomposition while retaining alloy homogeneity and surface composition.
A CoCrFeNi HEA exhibits element-dependent oxidation behavior and a partially oxidized surface in acidic solution under cathodic bias.
Particle size and surface defects could influence the measured effect of segregation on ethanol oxidation performance.
A lack of statistically significant degradation in activity, selectivity, and durability after induced segregation, or superior performance by the segregated catalyst, would falsify the hypothesis.
